headline: Why Abenomics Has Reversed, From Loosening to Tightening Monetary Policy?
summary: After more than a decade of low interest rates to fight deflation, Japan is changing course. Prolonged inflation, a weakening yen and rising fiscal pressure are cited as drivers.
why: Japan's monetary policy sets global yen funding costs and shapes carry trades. Shifts in Bank of Japan policy matter for Japanese bonds, the yen and global rates.
